summary: A cast-iron spark-plug tower on a reef in Fishers Island Sound, lit in 1884 to replace the Eel Grass Shoal lightship; privately owned since a 2010 auction.

access.note: Privately owned offshore tower; not open to the public.

events.note: Light established; Eel Grass Shoal lightship discontinued
Fifth-order lens replaced by fourth-order, dated 24 Dec 1898 in the 1899 report (LighthouseFriends says 1899)

corrections.why: Record's 1804 tower date appears to be an error; the lighthouse replaced a lightship in 1884. A USCG Historian search snippet says 'Station Established: 1804' but that page was not read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS lists fourth order; the 1884 notice and the 1899 report indicate a fifth-order original replaced in Dec 1898/1899.

notes_for_editor: NRHP nomination PDF not digitised (22 KB placeholder); NRHP listing taken from NPGallery metadata. Footnote numbers skip 5. Many details (Noyes background, Smith log, 2010 sale, 1954 automation, 1983 lens, Andrews incident) rest on LighthouseFriends only. The 1938 bulletin reading is from interleaved two-column OCR; Latimer Reef matched to the September 21 hurricane damage list by column position. 1891-92 volume printed page unconfirmed; cited by scan page. Record says built 1804; likely wrong. The 1892 report places the station 'off Mystic, Connecticut'; NY per NRHP metadata. Fact-check 2026-10-27: 1938 entry confirmed on page image (printed p.136, 'principal damage' in Long Island Sound, after the 21 Sept hurricane). Lens change dated 24 Dec 1898 in the 1899 report.
